problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${tan}^{2}⁡x{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x-1?$

examples.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring and Using Various Forms of the Secant-Tangent Identity
examples.problem: Express $\tan^2 x\sec^2 x - \tan^4 x +1$ in terms of $\sec x$ only.
examples.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x-1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(3),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{tan}^{2}⁡x{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{4}⁡x+1 & ={tan}^{2}⁡x({sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x)+1 \\  & ={tan}^{2}⁡x\cdot (1)+1 \\  & ={tan}^{2}⁡x+1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can use $(1),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{tan}^{2}⁡x+1 & ={sec}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\tan^2 x\sec^2 x - \tan^4 x +1 = \sec^2 x.
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x-1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(3),$ as follows:

$$
\frac{1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x}=\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x}
$$

Now, we factor the numerator as a difference of squares, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x} & =\frac{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x)(\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\operatorname{tan}⁡x)}{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x)}(\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\operatorname{tan}⁡x)}{\cancel{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x)}} \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\operatorname{tan}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x}=\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\operatorname{tan}⁡x.
$$
